nodes.title: Prompt Templates/Examples
widgets_values:
.: V2V Editing (replace a character in a target video) --- NOTE: TENDS TO LOOK BETTER ON SINGLE PASS. SEE OPTION ABOVE ---

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the girl whose motion comes from <Video 1> and whose appearance comes from <Picture 1>.
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. The girl's appearance is styled from <Picture 1>. Her motion, camera movement, background, and lighting from the video are preserved continuously from start to finish without deviation at any point.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - the girl's face, body proportions, and skin tone from <Picture 1> are retained, and her motion, choreography, rhythm, and timing from <Video 1> are retained at every moment. 
<Video 1> (whole-video temporal structure, motion path, camera movement, background, lighting): fully_preserved - the girl's choreography, movement speed, gestures, body positions, camera framing, camera movement, background, and lighting from every frame of <Video 1> are preserved throughout the entire target video without deviation.

detailed_description:
The target video uses a naturalistic style matching the source footage, preserving its original lighting, color grading, and camera work.
[Shot 1] The camera follows <Subject 1>, the girl, as she exists in the same setting from <Video 1>. Her appearance matches <Picture 1> — same skin tone, body shape, and natural contours. Throughout the entire video, her motion is a frame-by-frame motion match to <Video 1>: the same choreography, gestures, limb positions, movement speed, and rhythm are followed continuously from start to finish. The camera framing, angle, and movement stay locked to <Video 1> at all times. The background remains identical and unchanged.


.: Reference Generation (general filmmaking):

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the character in <Picture 1>. (basic description)

<Subject 2> is the scene location in <Picture 2>. (basic scene description)

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] highly realistic live-action scene of <Subject 1> in <Subject 2>.

retention_analysis:
<Audio 1>: reference - its vocal timbre guides the vocal delivery of <Subject 1> without copying the original signal.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1]: a close up shot of <Subject 1> with a shocked expression as the camera pulls in towards her face. Suddenly, she turns around to look behind her.
[Shot 2]: a 3/4ths shot of <Subject 1> as she turns, her expression is confused. She tilts her head to one side, a look of questioning. She hesitantly says using <Audio 1> as her vocal-timbre reference: <d>[English]Hello?.. Is anyone there?</d> her tone is hesitant and suspicious.
[Shot 3]: an over-the-shoulder following shot as <Subject 1> begins to walk through <Subject 2> looking around side to side.
 
overall_soundscape:
interior ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

nodes.title: Original template instructions (legacy)
widgets_values:
# MiniMax H3 Workflow Refactor

> **Design philosophy:** The user should control meaningful settings, while the workflow handles the internal routing, dependencies, and consequences automatically.

---

## Instructions

### 1. Prepare the Load Nodes

Disable any load nodes you're not using. Load media into every node you are using.

### 2. Configure the Control Panel

Use the **Control Panel** for the main workflow settings.

Set:

- Resolution
- Duration
- Reference counts
- Reference toggles
- Video Continuation
- Force Audio
- Final Upscale
- Interpolation
- Sparse Attention / VRAM options
- Sampler-related options

The workflow will handle the internal routing automatically based on those controls.

### 3. Configure References

Enable the references you want to use from the **Control Panel**.

You do not need to manually bypass individual reference groups.

Load the media you want to use into the corresponding:

- `<Picture>` reference nodes
- `<Audio>` reference nodes
- `<Video>` reference nodes

Only the references enabled by the controls are used for generation.

### 4. Set Video Reference Resolution Limits

When using a **video reference**, set the **Width** and **Height** values in the corresponding **Load Video** node to the maximum dimensions you want the reference video to use.

For example:

```text
Width: 768
Height: 768
Maintain Aspect Ratio: Selected

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the adult woman in the composite <Picture 1>. Use <Picture 1> only for her appearance: her facial identity, layered brown-and-pink hair, red clown nose, curled black false mustache, makeup, striped white blouse, and visible accessories. Do not copy its framing, poses, full-body views, or gray studio backdrop.
<Picture 3> is the strong setting, position, and composition reference for [Shot 1]. Match its camera, framing, and her placement exactly, from the first frame to the last.
<Audio 1> is the supplied speaking recording for <Subject 1> (S1). Reuse the complete recording as the final audio track, preserving its exact words, original language, voice, delivery, pauses, and timing. Synchronize her lips to its speech.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reuse] From the very first frame, <Subject 1> is positioned exactly as in <Picture 3> and speaks directly to the camera using <Audio 1>. Her appearance comes from <Picture 1>, and the setting, framing, and her position come from <Picture 3>. The camera remains static.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - preserve her referenced identity, clothing, hair, makeup, and accessories while animating her speech.
<Picture 3> (setting, framing, and position throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the camera angle, crop, scale, her centered placement, and the rainbow panel background exactly as shown, from the first frame through the last.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - reuse the complete supplied recording as the complete final audio track, with no added sounds.

detailed_description:
Photorealistic live-action rendering with natural skin, hair, and fabric textures. One locked-off, eye-level medium close-up in widescreen 16:9, identical in framing to <Picture 3> on every frame.

[Shot 1] Show <Subject 1> (S1), the adult woman from <Picture 1>, exactly as framed in <Picture 3>. Her face is centered horizontally. Her eyes sit just under one third of the way down from the top of the frame, the top of her hair nearly touches the top edge, her chin falls at about the halfway point of the frame, and her face, from forehead to chin, fills roughly one third of the frame height. Her shoulders span a little over half of the frame width, with background visible on both sides, and the bottom edge crops at her upper chest. Her body faces forward and her gaze meets the lens. The framing is no wider and no tighter than <Picture 3>: no waist, hands, furniture, or room are visible, and there is no extra space above her head.

Preserve <Picture 1>'s facial identity, brown hair over pink bangs and curls, red clown nose, curled black mustache, makeup, and striped white blouse. The reference's character design remains consistent when her mouth moves. Preserve the recognizable striped pattern, collar, and visible accessories within the established crop.

The background is the one in <Picture 3>: tall dark vertical panels with narrow divisions and soft rainbow gradients. A bright red-orange-yellow glow shades through green and cyan into deep blue on the left third of the frame, a thin glowing rainbow line sits near the left-center, a dark olive-gray panel is behind her head, a soft red glow is behind her on frame right, and a deep blue panel fills the far right. The panels stay fixed and keep the same positions relative to her head and shoulders.

She speaks the actual content of <Audio 1>, with lip shapes, jaw movement, syllable timing, pauses, and sentence endings synchronized to the recording. Her vocal tone and emotion follow the supplied audio. Facial movements remain natural for that delivery, while her head position, shoulder position, and distance from the camera stay consistent. Her false mustache remains attached and follows the movement of her upper lip.

Hold the camera at the same position, height, angle, and focal length throughout. Maintain the same framing without reframing between phrases. Keep her gaze directed toward the lens as she speaks, allowing speech-related expression while preserving the strong positional match to <Picture 3>. Finish with exactly the same framing, background alignment, and character appearance as the first frame.

nodes.title: Continuation mode: ON = REFRESHING (fresh gen + resample head), OFF = CLASSIC (guide + flat blend)
Guide (ON = no guide / refreshing, OFF = classic continuation guide)
Continuation mode switch
widgets_values:
**Continuation mode** (one boolean drives the guide switch and the head switch)

**OFF = classic:** `Guide for 1st Pass` conditions the generation on the uploaded clip's last N frames; the flat 0.5 `ImageBlend` joins the overlap.

**ON = refreshing:**
1. Fresh generation from your guides and prompt (no continuation guide).
2. The previous clip's last N frames are overlaid on the fresh gen's first N frames (old weight 1 -> 0 across the overlap), encoded, noised to HALF strength and denoised again (denoise 0.5), between two single-frame pins: the previous clip's first tail frame pins the START and the fresh gen's last overlap frame pins the END. The overlay carries the motion hand-over; the half-strength denoise merges the two takes into one. No mask, no taper, no hold.
3. Output = regenerated head + the rest of the fresh gen.

Two sampler passes run in this mode. If the resample does not run, check that the head switch is not bypassed.

**Landing guide** (inside the Refreshing group): a second guide pins the END of the resample window to the fresh gen's last overlap frame (same node, `frame_idx` -1, like the First and Last Frame subgraph). Switch it OFF to compare.

nodes.title: Initial generation (no previous clip)
widgets_values:
**To generate the first clip:** in the yellow bypass panel, switch OFF **Seamless Continuation** and **Refreshing mode** (they go together; the second only works with the first).

**References:** the clip is driven by three reference photos (`<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, `<Picture 3>`), named in the prompt. There is no mask or edge lock anymore.

nodes.title: Mode: head (ON = resampled head / refreshing, OFF = flat 0.5 blend / classic)
RESAMPLE: landing frame = fresh gen's last overlap frame
Landing guide: ON = also pin the end of the overlap, OFF = start guide only
RESAMPLE: START frame = previous clip's first tail frame
CROSSFADE weight of the OLD clip: 1.0 -> 0.0 (end index = Overlap Frames - 1 = 38)
OVERLAY: previous clip's tail over the fresh gen's head (old weight 1 -> 0)
PARTIAL DENOISE: denoise 0.5 (keep steps = 8 x denoise)

<Subject 1> is the adult woman in the composite <Picture 1>. Use <Picture 1> only for her appearance: her facial identity, layered brown-and-pink hair, red clown nose, curled black false mustache, makeup, striped white blouse, and visible accessories. Do not copy its framing, poses, full-body views, or gray studio backdrop.
<Picture 3> is the strong setting, position, and composition reference for [Shot 1]. Match its camera, framing, and her placement exactly, from the first frame to the last.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - preserve her referenced identity, clothing, hair, makeup, and accessories while animating her speech.
<Picture 3> (setting, framing, and position throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the camera angle, crop, scale, her centered placement, and the rainbow panel background exactly as shown, from the first frame through the last.

detailed_description:
Photorealistic live-action rendering with natural skin, hair, and fabric textures. One locked-off, eye-level medium close-up in widescreen 16:9, identical in framing to <Picture 3> on every frame.

[Shot 1] Show <Subject 1> (S1), the adult woman from <Picture 1>, exactly as framed in <Picture 3>. Her face is centered horizontally. Her eyes sit just under one third of the way down from the top of the frame, the top of her hair nearly touches the top edge, her chin falls at about the halfway point of the frame, and her face, from forehead to chin, fills roughly one third of the frame height. Her shoulders span a little over half of the frame width, with background visible on both sides, and the bottom edge crops at her upper chest. Her body faces forward and her gaze meets the lens. The framing is no wider and no tighter than <Picture 3>: no waist, hands, furniture, or room are visible, and there is no extra space above her head.

Preserve <Picture 1>'s facial identity, brown hair over pink bangs and curls, red clown nose, curled black mustache, makeup, and striped white blouse. The reference's character design remains consistent when her mouth moves. Preserve the recognizable striped pattern, collar, and visible accessories within the established crop.

The background is the one in <Picture 3>: tall dark vertical panels with narrow divisions and soft rainbow gradients. A bright red-orange-yellow glow shades through green and cyan into deep blue on the left third of the frame, a thin glowing rainbow line sits near the left-center, a dark olive-gray panel is behind her head, a soft red glow is behind her on frame right, and a deep blue panel fills the far right. The panels stay fixed and keep the same positions relative to her head and shoulders.

She speaks the actual content of <Audio 1>, with lip shapes, jaw movement, syllable timing, pauses, and sentence endings synchronized to the recording. Her vocal tone and emotion follow the supplied audio. Facial movements remain natural for that delivery, while her head position, shoulder position, and distance from the camera stay consistent. Her false mustache remains attached and follows the movement of her upper lip.

Hold the camera at the same position, height, angle, and focal length throughout. Maintain the same framing without reframing between phrases. Keep her gaze directed toward the lens as she speaks, allowing speech-related expression while preserving the strong positional match to <Picture 3>. Finish with exactly the same framing, background alignment, and character appearance as the first frame.

nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
# 🎬 MiniMax H3 · long-video workflow
## START HERE

**The idea:** every clip is a **fresh generation** from your prompt + reference pictures + audio. Nothing is carried over from the previous clip's latents, so quality can't degrade clip after clip. To make a longer video, only the **join** between two clips is rebuilt (crossfade → re-sample → stitch).

### How this canvas is organised
Read it **left → right, top → bottom**. Every step has a **note above it** and a numbered **group**.

| Row | Steps |
|---|---|
| **1 · SETUP** (what you choose) | 1 Models · 2 Speed & LoRAs · 3 Video settings · 4 Pictures · 5 Audio · 6 Control panel · 7 Prompts |
| **2 · GENERATE** (one fresh clip) | 8 Build · 9 Sample · 10 Decode & preview |
| **3 · STITCH** (join to the previous clip) | 11 Seamless continuation · 12 Refreshing mode · 13 Assemble & save |

### Quick start
- **First clip:** Step 6 → yellow **[Option]** panel → switch **Seamless Continuation** and **Refreshing mode** OFF → Run. The clip is saved to `output/minimax/final/`.
- **Next clip:** switch both ON → Step 11A: load the previous clip and check **Overlap Frames** → update prompt / audio if needed → Run.

### Reading the colours
**Blue** = Setup · **Orange** = Generate · **Purple** = Stitch · **Yellow** = the two switchable [Option] groups · **Cyan** = picture groups · **Green** = audio group.
Tiny collapsed `Set_…` / `Get_…` nodes are invisible wires: a *Set* publishes a value, *Get* nodes elsewhere read it by name.

widgets_values:
## Step 1 · Load models
Loads the four model files everything else uses.

| Node | File |
|---|---|
| Diffusion model | `MiniMax_H3_Ref2VA_pruned_int8_convrot` |
| Text encoder (CLIP) | `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq` |
| Video VAE | `minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot` |
| Audio VAE | `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32` |

The two VAEs are published as `vae` / `audio_vae` (Set nodes), so later steps read them with Get nodes.
**→ Feeds:** Step 2 (model), Steps 8 & 12 (CLIP), everything that encodes or decodes (VAEs).

nodes.title: Step 2 — speed & LoRAs
widgets_values:
## Step 2 · Speed, memory & LoRAs
The model passes through these patches in order (top-left → bottom-right):
1. **Model Options** – chunked feed-forward + low-VRAM attention (VRAM savers). Comfy-Kitchen attention is off.
2. **H3 Sparse Attention** – video attention budget 0.15 (faster).
3. **Sage Attention patch** – memory-efficient SageAttention.
4. **Turbo Sampler** – Turbo 8-step LoRA with sigma shift 12 (video) / 3 (audio).
5. **Power Lora Loader** – your own LoRA stack (check which slots are ON).

Each patch has its own ON / OFF switch inside the node. The Turbo LoRA is why Step 3 uses **8 steps**.
**→ Feeds:** `MODEL` → Step 3 (sigmas), Steps 9 & 12 (guiders, scheduler).

nodes.title: Step 3 — settings
widgets_values:
## Step 3 · Video settings & seed
Everything about size, length and sampler lives in **Video Settings**:
- **Sampler / scheduler / steps:** `er_sde` · `beta` · 8
- **Video length (seconds)** → snapped to a valid frame count (5 + 17·k) at 24 fps. 10 s → **243 frames**
- **Megapixels + aspect ratio** → width × height (multiples of 32). 0.4 MP @ 16:9 → **864 × 480** (size table on the right)
- **Match Audio to Duration:** ON = the video length follows the length of `<Audio 1>`

**Sampler Seed** (fixed) is shared by Step 9 and Step 12. The block publishes `width`, `height`, `duration`, `fps`, `SAMPLER` and `SIGMAS` for the other steps.

## Step 6 · Control panel
**Bypass panels** – one click toggles a whole group:
- **yellow [Option]** → Step 11 *Seamless Continuation* · Step 12 *Refreshing mode*
- **cyan Picture References** → the `<Picture n>` groups (Step 4)
- **green Audio References** → the `<Audio 1>` group (Step 5)

**Switches**
- **Force Audio** (ON) – injects your recording, VAE-encoded, as the audio latent so the voice follows it (Steps 8 & 12).
- **`<Picture 1>` is First Frame / `<Picture 2>` is Last Frame** (OFF) – pin a picture as the clip's first / last frame (Step 8C).
- **Use / Block `<Video 1>` Audio** (OFF) – legacy options for a reference video (Step 5).

**Remember:** first clip → both [Option] groups OFF · continuation clip → both ON.

nodes.title: Step 8 — build
widgets_values:
## Step 8 · Build the generation
Turns pictures + audio + prompt into the sampler's inputs. This is a **fresh generation** – nothing from the previous clip goes into the latent.
- **8A Reference-to-Video:** CLIP + VAEs + `<Picture n>` + `<Audio 1>` + prompt + width / height / length → `ref_positive` (conditioning) and an empty audio-video latent.
- **8B Starting latent:** split the video / audio latents, run **Force Audio**, re-join → `latent_image`.
- **8C Conditioning:** `ref_positive` → (Step 11 guide switch) → optional first / last-frame pins (both OFF) → `clip`, the guider's conditioning.

nodes.title: STEP 11 · SEAMLESS CONTINUATION — overview
widgets_values:
## Step 11 · Seamless continuation [Option]
Joins the new clip to the **previous clip**. Bypass this whole group (yellow panel, Step 6) to make a **first clip**.

**Continuation mode** (in 11D – one switch drives two places):
- **ON = Refreshing:** the new clip is a pure fresh generation; its first N frames are replaced by the **resampled head** from Step 12.
- **OFF = Classic:** the old tail is used as a **guide** for the first pass (11C) and the overlap is joined with a flat 50 / 50 blend.

**N = Overlap Frames** (11A): 5, 22 or 39 (= 5 + 17·k). 39 frames ≈ 1.6 s at 24 fps.
Flow: **A** load → **B** cut → **C** guide → *(Steps 8-10 generate)* → **D** blend the join → **E** stitch & audio → Step 13.

widgets_values_named.text:
## Step 11 · Seamless continuation [Option]
Joins the new clip to the **previous clip**. Bypass this whole group (yellow panel, Step 6) to make a **first clip**.

**Continuation mode** (in 11D – one switch drives two places):
- **ON = Refreshing:** the new clip is a pure fresh generation; its first N frames are replaced by the **resampled head** from Step 12.
- **OFF = Classic:** the old tail is used as a **guide** for the first pass (11C) and the overlap is joined with a flat 50 / 50 blend.

**N = Overlap Frames** (11A): 5, 22 or 39 (= 5 + 17·k). 39 frames ≈ 1.6 s at 24 fps.
Flow: **A** load → **B** cut → **C** guide → *(Steps 8-10 generate)* → **D** blend the join → **E** stitch & audio → Step 13.

nodes.title: STEP 12 · REFRESHING MODE — overview
widgets_values:
## Step 12 · Refreshing mode [Option]
Rebuilds the join instead of copying it. Used when **Continuation mode is ON** (11D).
1. **12A Overlay:** crossfade the old clip's last N frames (weight 1 → 0) over the new clip's first N frames and encode that overlay.
2. **12B Second Ref2V pass:** same pictures + audio + the second-pass prompt, for N frames; the first N frames of `<Audio 1>` are forced into the audio latent.
3. **12C Pin & denoise:** the old tail's first frame pins the **start**, the new clip's last overlap frame pins the **end** (*Landing guide*), then the overlay is re-sampled at **denoise 0.5** (4 of 8 steps) and decoded.

The result is the **resampled head** → Step 11D.

nodes.title: Step 13 — assemble & save
widgets_values:
## Step 13 · Assemble & save
Chooses what to save and writes the final MP4 (H.264, CRF 16, 24 fps) to `output/minimax/final/mm_<date>`.
- **Video:** the stitched result from Step 11 when that group is active, otherwise the plain generated clip (`repair_final` = decode from Step 10).
- **Audio:** same rule – Step 11's audio, otherwise `final_audio` from Step 10.

This is the only node that **saves**. For the next clip, load the saved file in Step 11A.
